title: Success by horizon: why long tasks are hard
design_ref: Why long horizons are hard; Measuring progress on long tasks
purpose: From the 128 root attempts of S02, measure success as a function of the number of bugs (the horizon), pass@1 against pass@4, the share of groups whose four attempts all agree (no learning signal for group-relative RL), partial progress on failures, recovery, the behaviour pathologies, and the environment time per solved task.

checks.description: success falls as the horizon grows
checks.because: Each added bug needs its own read, edit and test, and each is another chance to go wrong.

checks.description: pass@4 is above pass@1: the model can solve tasks it does not solve reliably
checks.because: pass@4 counts a task as solved if any of its four attempts was.

checks.description: many groups carry no signal for group-relative RL (all four attempts agree)
checks.because: When every attempt succeeds or every attempt fails, every advantage in the group is zero.
